chunks: And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih from Abu Ubaydah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had an Umm al-Walad (a slave woman who bore her master a child) and from him) and he had a son from her. When death approached him, he bequeathed for her two thousand dirhams or more, and instructed the heirs to enslave her. He (the Imam) said: 'No, rather she should be freed from one-third of the deceased's estate and given what he had bequeathed for her.'

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Umm al-Walad (a slave woman who bears her master a child)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an Umm al-Walad if her master bequeaths money to her and tells heirs to enslave her?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling to clarify the status of an Umm al-Walad when her master bequeaths a sum for her manumission but instructs heirs to enslave her; the Imam asserts that the specific bequest takes precedence, granting her freedom from the one-third estate share rather than reverting her to slavery. This highlights the Shia juristic preference for fulfilling the deceased's explicit financial intent to secure her liberty, distinguishing it from general manumission rules. The ruling underscores the dignity of the Umm al-Walad and the legal weight of bequests in securing her status within the family structure.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5507 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih from Abu Ubaydah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as), about a man who had a slave woman with whom he had a son. When death approached him, he bequeathed for her two thousand dirhams or more and instructed his heirs to enslave her.
Imam (as) said: "No, rather she should be freed from one-third of the deceased's estate and given what he had bequeathed for her."
